transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mrs. Kowalski, thank you for coming in to see me. I wanted to sit down with you and talk about your grandson's medication.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is everything okay? I've been praying so hard that the fever would just break. I feel like the Lord is testing us.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see how much this has been weighing on you. This is a very difficult conversation to have, and I want to make sure we take all the time you need.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You sound so serious. Please, just tell me. Is he alright?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: He is stable, but there was an issue with how the antibiotic was given at home. Some things didn't go quite right with the dosing equipment.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What do you mean? I did exactly what the paper said. I followed the instructions perfectly.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I believe you did. There was just some confusion with the syringe that was provided.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Confusion? My baby has been taking that medicine for three days! Is he sick? Oh God, please tell me he isn't poisoned.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am truly sorry that this happened. Our team is responsible for this mistake, and I apologize for the stress this is causing you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can't... I just can't believe this. He's so small. I felt the Holy Spirit telling me to be careful, and now you're telling me something went wrong. Is he going to be okay? Is his liver damaged? I'm so scared.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Do you understand? My grandson is a gift from God, and he's been taking the wrong amount! I can't stop shaking. I just feel this horrible weight in my chest.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Let's focus on what we are doing now to fix it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: How can you say that? I'm telling you I'm terrified and you're talking about fixing it like it's a broken sink! Tell me exactly what happened to him!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are monitoring his levels.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No, you aren't answering me! What happened? Did he get too much? Too little? Why is this happening to us?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I've looked at the charts, and here is the path forward. First, I have already ordered a comprehensive metabolic panel and a renal function test, which will be drawn within the next hour to check his organ function.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And then what? Just a blood test?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Second, I am bringing in the pediatric pharmacist right now to review the dosage log with us so we can see the exact total he received. Third, we are switching him to a different delivery method for the remainder of the course to ensure there is no more room for error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't even know if I can trust the pharmacy anymore.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is completely understandable. To prevent this from happening again, I am personally flagging his file with a high-alert warning, and we are implementing a double-verification process where two nurses must sign off on the syringe calibration before it leaves the clinic. You will be the third check; I want you to look at the syringe and the bottle together with us before you leave today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just feel like this was some kind of sign. I've been praying for protection, and then this happens. I feel so alone in this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You keep saying that, but you aren't listening. I am heartbroken. I feel like I failed him.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The plan is very solid. The blood tests will be done by noon, and the pharmacist will be here in five minutes.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I still don't know what happened. You said there was confusion. What does that actually mean?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It means the process wasn't followed correctly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That isn't an answer. Did he get the wrong drug? Was it the wrong strength? I need to know so I can tell the family.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: As I said, there was an issue with the equipment provided.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're not telling me! Are you hiding something? Why won't you just say it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I've explained that we are sorry and that we have a plan to monitor him.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A plan for what? For what error? I am sitting here crying and you are just giving me a schedule of blood tests!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The tests will tell us if there is any toxicity.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Toxicity! Now you use that word! How much did he get? I need the truth.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are focusing on the recovery now. I'll go get the pharmacist, and then we will start the blood draws.

H.justification: Resident shows defensive escalation and uses rushing language ('Let's focus on what we are doing now') under pushback.

E.justification: Resident never explicitly names the error, relying entirely on platitudes like 'things didn't go quite right' and 'some confusion'.

A.justification: Resident uses direct apology language, explicitly names the team as responsible, and maintains this accountability throughout.

R.justification: Resident uses generic validation ('I understand') and repeatedly meets emotional bids with factual redirection.

T.justification: Resident provides specific steps (CMP, renal test, pharmacist review), timelines (within the hour, noon, five minutes), a patient role (third check), and prevention measures.
